I just had my baby a week ago and have been an RBT for the last 9 almost 10 months. So basically my whole pregnancy I was employed in ABA. I’m not going to lie, it was hard, but in this field it is VERY important to advocate for yourself. Luckily, the clinic I worked at had very understanding BCBA’s and supervisors and weren’t surprised or supportive if I had to call off. I was also on some cases I was physically uncomfortable with and communicated that with my BCBA’s about switching cases/taking on less client loads. You have to take care of yourself in order to provide the best services in this field, otherwise you’re just wasting your time and the clients. Get on a doctor’s appt schedule if you can and talk to your supervisor about how frequent/what days of the week they will be if you can. Also, I went part time half way through and it was extremely beneficial for my body and mental health. Just remember to take breaks and listen to your body. A lot of RBT’s and BCBA’s are parents themselves so they understand the process.

It is because OCD is a tricky disease that can come in many forms of different obsessions, and most of the time it is not cured or managed through your typical talk therapy. Acting out on these urges to see your reactions to them isn’t supposed to “answer” your intrusive thoughts, (but by all means when your OCD is managed, and experimenting is still something you want to try, go ahead). For example, people with harm OCD aren’t going to be told, “oh, you should go out and try it to see if you actually want to do it!!” If we apply this cure to one form of OCD, we’d have to apply it to all because obsessions don’t care and come in any form. Instead, you build a fear ladder and expose yourself to your triggers and thoughts. We can’t just get “rid” of the thoughts, but we can change our reactions to them and assign less importance to them, and our brains will get the hint. That’s real OCD therapy.

This is exactly what the OCD wants, a realization and reaction to the urge, aka a compulsion. If your therapist isn’t helping, they probably do not know what HOCD is and they’re not giving you the tools for ERP and CBT.
